title: Handoff , an Agent Native Media Editor
pitch: A photo editor where every action is a real WebMCP tool so that an AI agent can crop, resize, and edit your images directly without any clicks.
about_excerpt:
A photo editor where every action is a real WebMCP tool so that an AI agent can crop, resize, and edit your images directly without any clicks.

 Inspiration 

 I work in developer support for a media/API company, and I spend a lot of
my day watching people struggle to get an AI agent to do something as
simple as "resize this and remove the background." The agent has to fake
mouse clicks through a UI that was built for us humans, it is slow and 
breaks the moment a button moves. When I saw this WebMCP Challenge, I thought about 
what if a webpage could just tell an agent what it can do, instead of making it guess. 

 What it does 

 Handoff is a photo editor where every action such as crop, resize, background
removal, text overlay, format conversion, export is registered as a
WebMCP tool via document.modelContext.registerTool() . 

 The same canvas, same underlying functions, can be driven two ways, 1. By a person
clicking buttons, or 2. By an AI agent working in English. Activity feed on the right side of the page tags every action as "You" Or "Agent". 

 How I built it 

 Very minimal coding, focused more on the outcome. 
Next.js on the frontend. 
Canvas API for crop, resize etc. 
 @imgly/background-removal for background removal. 
Every transformation happens on-device, in the browser, including the background-removal model itself. 

 I originally planned to build this on Cloudinary's media API, since
that's my day job. Eventually, decided to use the imgly background-removal. 

 Challenges I ran into 

 WebMCP wasn't detecting at all during testing. It turned out that the spec itself moved
 navigator.modelContext to document.modelContext on May 27, 2026, and
Chrome only deprecated the old location in Chrome 150. 
I added a fallback mechanism to handle both. 

 Accomplishments that I am proud of 

 All 8 tools are registered, schema-valid, and verified working
end-to-end. The whole tool runs with zero backend and zero API keys, which wasn't the
original plan but turned out to be the right constraint. 

 What I learned 

 I learned that in-browser AI (background removal via a client-side segmentation
model) is genuinely viable now, this runs comfortably in
a regular browser tab with no server round-trip. 

 What's next for Handoff 

 Next big step would be thumbnail extraction and trimming via ffmpeg.wasm for videos. Exploring batch operations and social media export presets as natural tools to register.
